events.title: Charles V Crowned Holy Roman Emperor
events.description: Charles V was crowned Holy Roman Emperor, taking the title at the head of a sprawling realm that spanned much of Europe and, through Spain, vast territories overseas.
events.significance: His reign joined the Habsburg, Spanish and Burgundian inheritances and shaped the Reformation era and the age of European colonial expansion.

events.title: First Continental Congress Adjourns
events.description: After weeks of debate in Philadelphia, delegates from the colonies concluded the First Continental Congress. They had coordinated a colonial response to British policies and agreed to meet again.
events.significance: The gathering was an early step in colonial unity, and it paved the way for the Second Continental Congress and the American Revolution.

events.title: The Football Association Is Founded
events.description: Representatives of London clubs and schools met and founded The Football Association, the first governing body for the sport. Its goal was to settle a common set of rules.
events.significance: The FA's rules helped separate association football from rugby and laid the foundations of the modern global game.

events.title: Gunfight at the O.K. Corral
events.description: In Tombstone, Arizona Territory, lawmen Wyatt, Virgil and Morgan Earp and Doc Holliday faced a group of outlaw Cowboys in a roughly 30-second shootout that left three men dead.
events.significance: The clash became one of the most famous episodes of the American Old West and a lasting symbol of frontier justice and legend.

events.title: Israel and Jordan Sign a Peace Treaty
events.description: Prime Ministers Yitzhak Rabin and Abdul-Salam Majali signed a formal treaty of peace between Israel and Jordan, ending decades of a declared state of war.
events.significance: Jordan became only the second Arab state to make peace with Israel, a landmark in Middle East diplomacy.
